title: Client-side resumable retention & adaptive timeout policy for partial streamed generations
creator: Liu Chen
description:
Problem: Clients frequently disconnect mid-generation (network flaps, mobiles sleeping, SDK crashes) creating partial generations and KV-cache fragments. Current behavior either keeps partial state indefinitely (wasteful) or aggressively GC immediately (causes poor UX when clients reconnect). We also need coordinated behavior when function/tool-calls are in-flight so you don't leave orphaned tool invocations or inconsistent structured outputs.

Goal: Implement a unified policy for soft retention, adaptive timeouts, and resumable tokens that: (1) preserves user-visible partial output for a short grace window, (2) avoids unbounded server-side resource hold, (3) coordinates function-call lifecycle so tool invocations are either completed or safely cancelled with clear audit events, and (4) remains compatible with existing SDKs and the hosted API.

Scope: Server-side runtime changes (lease + soft-ttl), resume token handshake in streaming protocol, SDK guards for reconnect/resume, backend compaction/cleanup job, and console observability bits. Out of scope for this ticket: multi-region long-term archival and paid retention plans.

Non-goals: This ticket is not implementing any new client UI for partial drafts; it focuses on protocol and server runtime guarantees and SDK primitives to enable UI work later.

acceptance_criteria: Server exposes lease token for each streaming generation containing: lease_id, expires_at, resumable=true|false.
Default soft retention policy configurable; default = 30s grace + 10min compaction window documented in runtime-1.21 release notes.
SDKs (JS and Python) can attempt a resume with lease token; resume succeeds if server-side prefix is intact and resumable=true.
Function/tool invocations started during a generation are annotated with lifecycle events and are either completed or marked cancelled before server compaction runs.
Console dashboard shows partial-output TTL histogram, active leases, and orphaned tool-call alerts.

Automated e2e tests covering: client disconnect -> reconnect resume success, client disconnect -> reconnect after compaction should fail gracefully with clear error code, orphaned tool-call detected and marked in audit log.
implementation_notes: Runtime: introduce lease manager table with partitioned TTL buckets to avoid hot compaction. Lease object = {lease_id, owner_sid, prefix_hash, resumable_flag, expires_at, last_heartbeat_at}.
Protocol: streaming handshake extension field `lease_token` returned on initial generation. SDKs store and offer token on reconnect with Resume command `X-Resume-Lease: <token>`.

Backpressure: when a client disconnects gracefully, server should move generation into 'soft-detached' state that continues allowing background tool completions for a short window but disallows new tokens without resume.
Tool-calls: mark long-running tool-call records with `non_resumable=true` if they allocate external resources; on compaction, emit cancel events and webhook to integrators.
Compaction job: incremental compaction respecting lease.expires_at; recompute KV-cache reference counts per prefix to avoid deleting shared cache entries prematurely.
SDKs: implement jittered lease-heartbeat attempts while connection idle; provide opt-in config `resumeOnReconnect: true|false` and fallback policies for older server versions.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Clients on old SDKs may not include resume tokens -> will fallback to creating a new generation and may duplicate costs. Mitigation: server will accept absent resume tokens and perform cheap prefix existence check; add telemetry for detecting old SDKs.
Risk: Lease table growth under heavy reconnect churn. Mitigation: compact leases into coarse buckets and apply write-through caching for hot prefixes; enforce per-account lease quotas.
Risk: Tool-call or external system confusion leading to duplicated side-effects. Mitigation: adopt idempotency keys for tool invocations and require integrators to honor cancel lifecycle events.
qa_plan: Unit tests for lease lifecycle transitions and compaction triggers.
Integration tests: simulated flaky network (disconnect/reconnect) validating resume semantics and function-call lifecycle.
Load test: create 10k short-lived connections with random disconnects and validate compaction latency and DB write amplification.
Manual: verify console dashboard alerts for orphaned tool-calls and sample audit trail entries.
